t2m_max_mean.model_description: Least-squares straight line through the training years
t2m_max_mean.interval_note: Nominal 80% empirical residual band; not a calibrated guarantee. Validation windows overlap; limited residual sample.
t2m_max_mean.summary_text: Average monthly maximum temperature in 2026–2030 is forecast to average 28.5 °C (nominal 80% band for 2030: 28.3–28.9 °C; coverage is not guaranteed), above the 1991–2020 average of 28.1 °C (+0.43 °C).

rh2m_mean.model_description: Recursive ridge regression on the previous three annual values (fixed L2=1)
rh2m_mean.interval_note: Nominal 80% empirical residual band; not a calibrated guarantee. Validation windows overlap; limited residual sample.
rh2m_mean.summary_text: Mean relative humidity in 2026–2030 is forecast to average 79.3 % (nominal 80% band for 2030: 78.8–80.6 %; coverage is not guaranteed), about the same as the 1991–2020 average of 79.2 %.

precip_dry_season.model_description: Least-squares straight line through the training years
precip_dry_season.interval_note: Nominal 80% empirical residual band; not a calibrated guarantee. Validation windows overlap; limited residual sample.
precip_dry_season.data_caution: Reanalysis rainfall is the least reliable NASA POWER variable. Several sites show large multi-year shifts (e.g. Bramble Cay 2015–2025 about 42 % drier than 1981–2014; Monteverde dry-season rain about 3 times higher in 2009–2025 than in 1981–2008). A change-point test places these shifts in different years (1998–2015), so they do not point to a single data-source switch, but they may still be partly artificial. Rainfall forecasts that extend such shifts are uncertain: show the 80 % range and verify against local rain gauges before presenting them as fact.
precip_dry_season.summary_text: Dry-season rainfall in 2026–2030 is forecast to average 126.9 mm (nominal 80% band for 2030: 43.8–500.1 mm; coverage is not guaranteed), below the 1991–2020 average of 134.7 mm (-7.78 mm).
